item.title: Analytical Interacting Tight-binding Model for Fractional Chern Insulators
item.description: arXiv:2611.23409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a two-dimensional 2-band tight-binding model with two-body interactions and without magnetic lattice translation, in which both the hopping and interaction are exponentially local (with Gaussian decay) in real space. Th…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.23409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a two-dimensional 2-band tight-binding model with two-body interactions and without magnetic lattice translation, in which both the hopping and interaction are exponentially local (with Gaussian decay) in real space. The interaction is built from pair annihilation operators whose coefficients are hopping amplitudes divided by positive powers of relative distance. Without any band projection, the ground states at $1/3$ filling are exactly fractional Chern insulator (FCI) states (and thus have nonzero gap) for any finite lattice size with any periodic/twist boundary conditions. The FCI ground states are analogous to the discretized version of the Laughlin-like states in the continuum Chern-ideal band, though our FCI states do not require the onsite spinor structure that is necessary in the continuum. We further show analytically that, after adding one unit cell while keeping electron number fixed, the anyonic one-quasihole states are zero-energy ground states of the full Hamiltonian for any finite system size and any quasihole position, analogous to Laughlin quasiholes under the Haldane $V_1$ pseudopotential. Numerical evidence is provided for the possible nonzero gap of the FCI states at $1/3$ filling in the thermodynamic limit, when interaction strength is much smaller than the single-particle band gap.

item.title: Synthesis-route-dependent state selection in the frustrated spinel ZnV$_2$O$_4$
item.description: arXiv:2611.23500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The emergent properties of strongly correlated materials can be highly sensitive to how they are made, yet synthesis pathway is rarely treated as a fundamental variable governing their ground states. The spinel ZnV$_2$O$_4$ provides…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.23500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The emergent properties of strongly correlated materials can be highly sensitive to how they are made, yet synthesis pathway is rarely treated as a fundamental variable governing their ground states. The spinel ZnV$_2$O$_4$ provides a model system in which to test this idea: its pyrochlore lattice of antiferromagnetically coupled V$^{3+}$ $S=1$ moments hosts competing spin and orbital degeneracies, while different synthesis routes yield markedly different low-temperature behaviour. Here, we show that changing the solid-state synthesis pathway reproducibly selects a distinct structural and magnetic ground state. Microwave-assisted solid-state synthesis (MASS) stabilises the cubic spinel structure to low temperature, suppressing the conventional cubic-to-tetragonal transition and preserving the highly frustrated $S=1$ pyrochlore lattice. Combining high-resolution diffraction, magnetometry and inelastic neutron scattering, we find a magnetic ground state exhibiting persistent spin-liquid-like dynamics together with partial spin freezing. Our results establish synthesis pathway as an experimental variable for selecting between competing emergent states in strongly correlated materials, revealing a route to accessing ground states not realised by conventional synthesis.

item.description: arXiv:2611.23842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In order to calculate the electronic structure of correlated materials, we propose implementation of the LDA+Gutzwiller method with Newton's method. The self-consistence process, efficiency and convergence of calculation are improve…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.23842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In order to calculate the electronic structure of correlated materials, we propose implementation of the LDA+Gutzwiller method with Newton's method. The self-consistence process, efficiency and convergence of calculation are improved dramatically by using Newton's method with golden section search and other improvement approaches. We compare the calculated results by applying the previous linear mix method and Newton's method. We have applied our code to study the electronic structure of several typical strong correlated materials, including SrVO$_3$, LaCoO$_3$, and La$_2$O$_3$Fe$_2$Se$_2$. Our results fit quite well with the previous studies.

item.title: Local spin constraints and symmetry in single-$Q$ spiral magnets
item.description: arXiv:2611.23882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Luttinger--Tisza (LT) method provides a lower bound on the energy of classical spin models but relaxes the local spin-length constraints. For a generic incommensurate single-$Q$ spiral, fixed spin length requires circular polari…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.23882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Luttinger--Tisza (LT) method provides a lower bound on the energy of classical spin models but relaxes the local spin-length constraints. For a generic incommensurate single-$Q$ spiral, fixed spin length requires circular polarization on every magnetic sublattice, a condition not guaranteed by equal sublattice weights in the lowest LT eigenmode. We develop a constrained formulation for general bilinear classical spin Hamiltonians with one or two magnetic sublattices. For one sublattice, minimization reduces to a secular equation for the spiral-plane normal. For two sublattices, exact elimination of the relative phase gives a frame-independent energy on the space of two unit normals. We derive symmetry constraints by distinguishing operations that preserve or reverse the Fourier arm and those that preserve or exchange sublattices. For a model with symmetric anisotropy, numerical optimization over both spiral-plane normals yields a lower energy than either constrained pure exchange-sector state, despite the block diagonalization of the linear Hamiltonian. A separate anisotropic two-sublattice benchmark demonstrates that enforcing local circularity can shift the preferred ordering wave vector even when the lowest LT eigenmode has equal sublattice weights.

item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.23918v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We theoretically predict a molecular Kondo ball in TiSc$_2$N@C$_{80}$/Al(111), where a Ti-centered $S = 1/2$ local moment is encapsulated within a closed fullerene $\pi$ cage that serves as an itinerant-like electronic reservoir for Kondo screening. item.title: Stabilizer models of achiral abelian topological orders
item.description: arXiv:2611.24105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct continuous-variable stabilizer codes realizing every achiral 2D abelian topological order, both bosonic and fermionic. Starting from an arbitrary signature-zero integer $K$-matrix, we show that the corresponding topolog…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.24105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct continuous-variable stabilizer codes realizing every achiral 2D abelian topological order, both bosonic and fermionic. Starting from an arbitrary signature-zero integer $K$-matrix, we show that the corresponding topological order can be obtained by condensing a lattice of dyons with trivial pairwise mutual braiding in an $\mathbb{R}^N$ gauge theory. We implement this condensation microscopically by gauging a non-on-site 1-form symmetry of the $\mathbb{R}^N$ toric code.

item.title: Hidden topological signatures in a van der Waals ferromagnet revealed by spin-resolved circular-dichroic photoemission
item.description: arXiv:2611.24468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Layered ferromagnets with strongly correlated electrons provide a platform for exploring the interplay among magnetism, spin-orbit coupling, and nontrivial band topology. $\mathrm{Ni}_{1/4}\mathrm{TaSe}_2$ is a correlated van der Wa…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.24468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Layered ferromagnets with strongly correlated electrons provide a platform for exploring the interplay among magnetism, spin-orbit coupling, and nontrivial band topology. $\mathrm{Ni}_{1/4}\mathrm{TaSe}_2$ is a correlated van der Waals ferromagnet with a transition temperature of 58 K that lies close in composition to a superconducting phase that emerges upon Ni depletion. Here, we combine spin- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, circular-dichroism measurements, and density functional theory calculations to investigate its spin-resolved electronic structure. We observe spin-polarized states crossing the Fermi level and signatures of broken time-reversal symmetry in the ferromagnetic state. Spin-resolved circular-dichroism measurements further reveal a helicity-dependent spin response consistent with a finite spin Berry curvature and suggestive of local topological character. Together, these results establish an experimental connection between ferromagnetism, spin-polarized electronic states, and topological signatures in $\mathrm{Ni}_{1/4}\mathrm{TaSe}_2$, providing a foundation for investigating how these properties may relate to the emergence of superconductivity upon Ni depletion.

item.title: From geometric curvature to effective backgrounds: a dictionary for Dirac fermions in one, two and three spatial dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.24878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dirac equation on curved backgrounds can be rewritten as a flat-space equation in which geometry appears as a tensorial Fermi velocity together with a set of background fields. We derive this correspondence from a single Clifford-al…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.24878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dirac equation on curved backgrounds can be rewritten as a flat-space equation in which geometry appears as a tensorial Fermi velocity together with a set of background fields. We derive this correspondence from a single Clifford-algebra identity and follow it through one, two, and three spatial dimensions. Once the spin connection is written in terms of Ricci rotation coefficients, only two contractions can occur. The trace produces a term with the index structure of a vector potential in every dimensionality; it enters with an imaginary factor i and is precisely the term that keeps the operator Hermitian when the Fermi velocity depends on position. The totally antisymmetric contraction produces an object that depends on the number of indices available to the Levi-Civita symbol: a trace on a line, a pseudoscalar mass on a surface, and an axial vector potential in a volume. Neither contraction is invariant under local rotations of the frame, and we give the transformation laws. On a surface, the curl of the trace term can always be removed by a frame rotation, while its divergence is proportional to the Gaussian curvature. We apply the correspondence to a Gaussian bump, where the local density of states at the center falls below its flat value and obeys a closed form at low energy; to a wire, where a nonuniform lapse binds states inside the gap and a nonuniform velocity cannot; to stationary frames on a surface, where a circulating drag shifts the Dirac mass locally with either sign; and to twisted and rotating frames in a volume, where the axial term takes the form of a chiral chemical potential produced by the frame alone, or separates Weyl nodes in a rotating sample. We separate the geometric contribution from the lattice pseudogauge field that dominates the response of strained samples

item.title: Exact Parent Hamiltonians for Partially Magnetized Chiral Spin Liquids
item.description: arXiv:2611.24935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chiral spin liquids (CSLs) are paradigmatic fractionalized phases, yet simple exact parent Hamiltonians for them remain scarce. In this work, we construct exact spin parent Hamiltonians for partially magnetized CSLs realizing variou…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.24935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chiral spin liquids (CSLs) are paradigmatic fractionalized phases, yet simple exact parent Hamiltonians for them remain scarce. In this work, we construct exact spin parent Hamiltonians for partially magnetized CSLs realizing various bosonic topological orders. Our construction relies on an exact Hubbard-type parent Hamiltonian for bosonic lattice fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states, valid at arbitrary repulsive interaction strengths. Taking the on-site repulsion to infinity and applying local boson-spin mappings yields exact parent Hamiltonians for the CSLs. Our two-spin construction generalizes the Kalmeyer-Laughlin spin Hamiltonian to a broader class of bosonic FQH model states, including Abelian states and non-Abelian parton states. We derive controlled microscopic realizations of these two-spin Hamiltonians via second-order superexchange in generalized spinful Hofstadter-Hubbard models with tailored hoppings and interactions. With more general local constraints and interactions, boson-spin mappings yield exact higher-spin and multispin parent Hamiltonians for partially magnetized CSLs.

item.title: Trapped fermions frustrate multiterminal Josephson networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.23390v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coherent control of fermions has become a standard approach for engineering quantum devices. Here, we explore parity-induced frustration in multiterminal Josephson arrays. We focus on odd-parity Josephson trijunctions, where the p…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.23390v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coherent control of fermions has become a standard approach for engineering quantum devices. Here, we explore parity-induced frustration in multiterminal Josephson arrays. We focus on odd-parity Josephson trijunctions, where the presence of a trapped fermion induces a phase winding in each trijunction. Connecting these trijunctions constrains their shared phases, resulting in a long-distance phase coherence where the frustrated configurations dominate the low-energy physics. In the classical regime, these arrays map onto the Kagome XY antiferromagnet, whose established Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition yields algebraically decaying $6e$ phase correlations. We show that the $6e$ phase coherence is manifested as a pronounced third harmonic in the current-phase relation of these arrays. While quantum phase fluctuations suppress the $6e$ coherence, we show that through spin-orbit coupling they also lead to spin correlations and entanglement between the trapped fermions. Our results establish fermion-induced frustration as a route to composite superconducting coherence and phase-mediated spin entanglement in superconductor-semiconductor artificial quantum materials.

item.title: Quantum resources and the onset of the quantum Monte Carlo sign problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.23514v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Monte Carlo sign problem poses a fundamental obstacle to classical simulation of quantum many-body systems, yet its connection to quantum resources remains poorly understood. We probe this connection by systematically tuning t…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.23514v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Monte Carlo sign problem poses a fundamental obstacle to classical simulation of quantum many-body systems, yet its connection to quantum resources remains poorly understood. We probe this connection by systematically tuning the degree of nonstoquasticity in random k-local Hamiltonians. In numerical tensor-network studies, we find the sign complexity and the quantum resources of entanglement and nonstabilizerness of the ground state to be strongly suppressed in a broad regime up to substantial nonstoquasticity. As nonstoquasticity is further increased, the considered quantum resources experience sharp crossovers into a regime where they are strongly enhanced. Surprisingly, numerical quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations drastically deteriorate in the same region, even though the Hamiltonian is already considerably nonstoquastic well before it, indicating that the failure of ground-state QMC is correlated more with the resource content of the state than the sign structure of the Hamiltonian. We corroborate these findings analytically by constructing an approximate ground state of k-local Hamiltonians in the stoquastic limit. Moreover, we identify a distinct behaviour in graph states. Their nonstabilizerness always vanishes, but, as we demonstrate analytically, on bipartite graphs the sign can be easily cured while in multipartite graph states it cannot. Our results thus shed light on the highly subtle interplay between quantum resources and the computational difficulty encountered by QMC methods.

item.title: Layer-dependent $s^{\pm}$ superconducting pairing and influence of incipient bands in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ thin films on real LaSrAlO$_4$ substrate
item.description: arXiv:2611.23595v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by recent advances in ambient-pressure superconducting La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ (LNO) thin films, we theoretically investigate these films by explicitly incorporating the realistic LaSrAlO$_4$ (LSAO) substrate. The Fermi-surfac…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.23595v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by recent advances in ambient-pressure superconducting La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ (LNO) thin films, we theoretically investigate these films by explicitly incorporating the realistic LaSrAlO$_4$ (LSAO) substrate. The Fermi-surface topology of the nickelate thin film closely resembles that of the high-pressure bulk phase, with similar $\alpha$ and $\beta$ sheets and a small hole-like $\gamma$ pocket originating from the surface bilayer (BL3). The bonding $d_{3z^2-r^2}$ state of the interfacial bilayer (BL1, adjacent to the LSAO substrate) lies only $\sim 5$ meV below the Fermi level, giving rise to an incipient $\gamma$ band, while for the middle bilayer (BL2) its energy is much lower ($\sim 95$ meV). Remarkably, no significant spontaneous charge transfer from the LSAO substrate to the LNO film is found. Instead, {\it symmetry-allowed charge disproportionation} occurs between the BLs, with hole doping in BL3 and electron doping in BL1 and BL2. Via the weak-coupling Random Phase Approximation, we find a strong $s^{\pm}$-wave superconducting pairing instability in BL3, while $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $s^{\pm}$ are nearly degenerate in the other bilayers BL1 and BL2. Including the incipient $\gamma$ band via the Dynamical Cluster Approximation beyond weak coupling, robust $s^{\pm}$-wave pairing is observed in all three layers

item.title: Addressable transversal CCZ gates on almost good quantum LDPC codes and nearly optimal magic state protocols
item.description: arXiv:2611.23762v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Assuming uniform subfield product expansion, we construct quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes with distances $\Omega_\epsilon(N/\log^2N)$ and at least $N^{1-\epsilon}$ individually addressable logical CCZ gates on pairw…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.23762v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Assuming uniform subfield product expansion, we construct quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes with distances $\Omega_\epsilon(N/\log^2N)$ and at least $N^{1-\epsilon}$ individually addressable logical CCZ gates on pairwise disjoint triples of logical qubits, for every fixed $0<\epsilon<1$. With all logical qubits outside these triples initialized to $|0\rangle$, any subset of the corresponding logical CCZ gates can be implemented with a transversal physical CCZ circuit. As applications, we obtain two nearly optimal magic state protocols: CCZ distillation with arbitrarily small overhead exponent $\gamma \rightarrow 0$ and error suppression of nearly linear order, and a magic state fountain that directly prepares $N^{1-\epsilon}$ encoded CCZ magic states with nearly linear distance $\Omega_\epsilon(N/\log^2N)$. The construction uses balanced products of expanding graph covers. The assumption concerns Reed--Solomon codes on three subfields of characteristic two and pairwise coprime extension degrees, a local hypothesis studied in a companion manuscript. We design the expanding graph covers to admit many common classical codewords, which yield logical operators whose pairings select the logical CCZ gates independently. Without the product expansion assumption, the graph covers also yield classical LDPC codes over a fixed field with almost linear dimension and linear distance that satisfy a multiplication property: the coordinatewise product of any three codewords lies in a second LDPC code of linear distance.

item.title: Non-Abelian Hall Effects of Flavor-Waves in $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ Skyrmions
item.description: arXiv:2611.24134v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the collective excitations of isolated and crystalline $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ skyrmions in a two-dimensional triangular-lattice spin-1 magnet. Within an $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ coherent-state framework, fluctuations of the magn…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.24134v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the collective excitations of isolated and crystalline $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ skyrmions in a two-dimensional triangular-lattice spin-1 magnet. Within an $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ coherent-state framework, fluctuations of the magnetic dipole and quadrupole moments are described by two coupled bosonic flavors. In a uniform spin-polarized state, these flavors can be identified with single-spin-flip and double-spin-flip excitations, whereas a nonuniform $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ texture mixes their character. We formulate the corresponding bosonic Bogoliubov--de Gennes problem and examine the matrix-valued gauge connection governing flavor-wave propagation. For isolated skyrmions, the calculated spectrum contains localized modes, and the scattering dynamics exhibit transverse deflection accompanied by isospin precession. For a numerically relaxed skyrmion crystal, we obtain collective-mode bands with nonzero Chern numbers and calculate the associated thermal Hall response. These findings illustrate how projective magnetic textures couple multipolar excitations to non-Abelian transport and topological band phenomena.

item.title: Reconciling Models for Infinite-Layer Nickelate Superconductors: Role of Interstitial-$s$ Band or $A$-Pocket
item.description: arXiv:2611.24288v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Understanding the minimal model that captures the essential physics of infinite-layer nickelate superconductors remains a central challenge. Using first-principles density-functional theory combined with dynamical mean-field theor…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.24288v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Understanding the minimal model that captures the essential physics of infinite-layer nickelate superconductors remains a central challenge. Using first-principles density-functional theory combined with dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT), we compute and compare the strongly correlated electronic structures and optical spectra of various effective models for the infinite-layer nickelate LaNiO$_2$, ranging from a $d_{x^2-y^2}$ 1-band model to a full 6-band model with all Ni-$3d$ plus an interstitial-$s$ orbital. The results demonstrate that Ni-$3d$ 5-band models overestimate the Hundness picture, whereas 6-band models, which explicitly include the interstitial-$s$ band and have an $A$-pocket, recover the characteristic Mottness physics. Importantly, the influence of the interstitial-$s$ band on the correlations of the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ band is negligible. Thus, superconductivity in infinite-layer nickelates can be reliably described within a single-band Hubbard framework, while the accurate description of inter-orbital properties such as (optical) conductivities requires the inclusion of at least the interstitial-$s$ band.

item.title: Conformal defects in a quasi-one-dimensional Kitaev chain: an exactly parametrized Ising defect line and a relevant vacancy
item.description: arXiv:2611.24312v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The quasi-one-dimensional Kitaev chain of coupled hexagonal plaquettes recently introduced by Majumder is exactly solvable in terms of free Majorana fermions and undergoes a topological transition at the exchange anisotropy $J_x=\…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.24312v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The quasi-one-dimensional Kitaev chain of coupled hexagonal plaquettes recently introduced by Majumder is exactly solvable in terms of free Majorana fermions and undergoes a topological transition at the exchange anisotropy $J_x=\sqrt{2}\,J$. By eliminating the two-coordinated sites of each plaquette we reduce the zero-energy problem to a uniform Majorana chain, which yields the critical point, a single Majorana cone at $k=0$ (hence an Ising critical point with central charge $c=\tfrac12$), and closed forms for every defect quantity that follows. A weakened inter-plaquette bond $\lambda J_x$ is an exactly marginal defect with transmission $T=4\lambda^2/(1+\lambda^2)^2$ at low energy, that is, $T=\sin^2 2\phi$ with $\tan\phi=\lambda$: the bond traverses the ferromagnetic defect line of the Ising conformal field theory from the transparent point to the cut chain, and we give its exact energy dependence on the lattice. The intra-plaquette bonds land on the same line with different parametrizations: a $y$ or $z$ bond has $\tan\phi=(1+\lambda)/2$ and covers only $T\in[0.64,1]$, because the plaquette provides a parallel path, whereas an $x$ bond has $\tan\phi=(1+\lambda)/2\lambda$ and covers the strong-link half of the line, $\phi\in(\pi/4,\pi/2)$. The identification is closed by an independent observable: the coefficient of $\ln L$ in the entanglement entropy across the defect follows the conformal-field-theory function $\sigma(\sqrt T)/2$ of Brehm and Brunner to within $0.4\%$ along the whole line, with no adjustable parameter. A vacancy behaves in the opposite way. It never binds a plaquette flux, because plaquettes share no sites, but it leaves its singly bonded neighbor as a conserved classical spin whose dangling Majorana is a zero-energy resonance.

item.title: $1/N$ corrections to $\langle TJJ\rangle$ and $\langle TTT\rangle$ in QED$_3$, QED$_3$--GNY and scalar QED$_3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.24531v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Three-dimensional Abelian gauge theories have broad applications in deconfined quantum criticality, Dirac spin liquids and cuprate superconductivity. Correlation functions of conserved currents $J$ and the stress tensor $T$ carry …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.24531v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Three-dimensional Abelian gauge theories have broad applications in deconfined quantum criticality, Dirac spin liquids and cuprate superconductivity. Correlation functions of conserved currents $J$ and the stress tensor $T$ carry fundamental information about these theories. We compute the first subleading large-flavor corrections to the parity-even three-point functions $\langle TJJ\rangle$ and $\langle TTT\rangle$ in QED$_3$, QED$_3$--Gross--Neveu--Yukawa, and critical scalar QED$_3$. For $\langle TJJ\rangle$, we study both global flavor currents and the topological $U(1)$ current, which measures the magnetic flux of the dynamical gauge field. We evaluate the flat-space energy flux in directions where the leading free-field profile vanishes. At first subleading order the flux in these directions is determined by four-particle production, yielding analytic corrections to the conformal collider parameters. We reproduce the corrections independently from squashed-sphere free-energy derivatives. Together with known two-point normalizations, the collider parameters fix the coefficients of both independent tensor structures in each correlator. Our results are useful for studying conductivity and shear response near quantum critical points and for conformal bootstrap studies of conserved-current and stress-tensor correlators in strongly coupled gauge theories.

item.title: Gutzwiller Quantum-Classical Embedding for Dynamics Simulations of Correlated Electron Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.24592v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Simulating the real-time dynamics of correlated electron systems requires a nonperturbative treatment of local correlations over long times, a challenge for classical methods. We present the time-dependent Gutzwiller quantum-class…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.24592v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Simulating the real-time dynamics of correlated electron systems requires a nonperturbative treatment of local correlations over long times, a challenge for classical methods. We present the time-dependent Gutzwiller quantum-classical embedding framework, t-GQCE, for generic multi-orbital lattice models with time-dependent Hamiltonians. Within the time-dependent ghost Gutzwiller approximation, the lattice dynamics is mapped onto a noninteracting quasiparticle lattice, propagated classically, coupled to finite interacting embedding models propagated on quantum processors. The two parts exchange only embedding Hamiltonian parameters and single-particle density matrices, and the framework is agnostic to the quantum dynamics solver. We demonstrate it with adaptive variational quantum dynamics simulations of interaction quenches in the Hubbard model on the Bethe lattice. Without ghost orbitals, the embedding problem reduces to a single qubit, simulated on IBM quantum hardware with two qubits, including an ancilla. With more ghost orbitals, t-GQCE suppresses the artificial undamped oscillations of the conventional Gutzwiller approximation and approaches nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory results for weak and strong quenches. Statevector simulations with 2, 4 and 6 ghost orbitals per spin, or 8, 12 and 16 qubits, give adaptive circuits that follow the embedding states with infidelities below $5\times10^{-4}$. Under trapped-ion noise models, circuit compression, measurements in rotated orbital bases with post-selection, and noise mitigation reduce the measurement errors severalfold. At one third of the error rates of a hardware-benchmarked noise model, they reach an accuracy of $0.01$ for the single-particle density matrix and the double occupancy with $10^5$ shots per time step, and the Quantinuum H2-Emulator gives similar accuracy.

item.title: The magical memory cost of entanglement spectrum compression
item.description: arXiv:2611.24710v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How much quantum memory is needed to faithfully retain the entanglement spectrum of a bipartite pure state after separating out Bell pairs through local unitaries? We derive the exact tradeoff between Bell-pair yield, residual mem…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.24710v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How much quantum memory is needed to faithfully retain the entanglement spectrum of a bipartite pure state after separating out Bell pairs through local unitaries? We derive the exact tradeoff between Bell-pair yield, residual memory, and reconstruction fidelity under local unitaries, defining an operational measure of entanglement-spectrum complexity. Smoothed entanglement spread bounds this memory cost from below, while diverging nonlocal magic forces unbounded memory at any fixed positive fidelity. Chaotic circuit dynamics exhibit a transient memory peak whose height increases with system size, followed by declining cost despite continued entropy growth. A large typical Haar-random state requires only an accuracy-dependent memory, whereas stationary fermionic Gaussian states retain a growing cost with size. In the circuits studied, the multiscale spectral structure associated with entanglement catalysis also has a practical consequence for matrix product state compression, yielding a multiplicative overhead not captured by the conventional entropy-based bond dimension estimate.

item.title: An Atiyah--Hirzebruch to Adams map and the hastened Adams spectral sequence for supercohomology
item.description: arXiv:2611.24725v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a map of filtered spectra inducing a map from the Atiyah--Hirzebruch spectral sequence (AHSS) to the Baker--Lazarev Adams spectral sequence of a $\mathit{ko}$-module $M$. Using this and a theorem of Bruner--Rognes, we…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.24725v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a map of filtered spectra inducing a map from the Atiyah--Hirzebruch spectral sequence (AHSS) to the Baker--Lazarev Adams spectral sequence of a $\mathit{ko}$-module $M$. Using this and a theorem of Bruner--Rognes, we construct a hastened Adams spectral sequence (HASS) for the Postnikov truncations of $\mathit{ko}$ and the connective Adams summand. Then, motivated by questions in quantum field theory, topological phases of matter, and tensor category theory, we apply the HASS to supercohomology, the cohomology theory $I_{\mathbb{C}^\times}(\tau_{\le 2}\mathit{ko})$, and observe that in examples of interest it is easier to calculate with than either the AHSS or the usual Adams spectral sequence. We include a User's Guide to the HASS and several worked examples, as well as hastened Adams charts for many commonly encountered $\mathcal{A}(1)$-modules.

item.title: Learning the Anyon Atlas
item.description: arXiv:2611.24752v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend our previous search for the modular data of topological quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions from 22 to 42 anyons, identifying 150,679 new modular data. We do so by adding to our algorithm three rejection gates, two …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.24752v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend our previous search for the modular data of topological quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions from 22 to 42 anyons, identifying 150,679 new modular data. We do so by adding to our algorithm three rejection gates, two of them based on logistic regression, that discard representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ unlikely to yield modular data. We estimate that roughly 80% of the modular data between ranks 23 and 42 has been identified after closing under known constructions. With this data, we find counterexamples to a conjecture of Geiko and Moore that the reality of the higher Gauss sums suffices for time-reversal symmetry in Chern-Simons theories, and propose a refined criterion. We demonstrate the scalability of this gated implementation by identifying prime modular data at rank 100 that is not realized by any Chern-Simons theory. The identified data through rank 42 has been made available at https://AnyonAtlas.org, to which further data will be added as it is found.

item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.24753v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a strategy for computing the $F$-symbols of unitary modular categories with a self-dual simple generator, starting from their modular data, which almost entirely avoids the non-linear solution of the pentagon equations. The algorithm climbs a ladder of braid group representations on successively more strands of the generator until enough $F$-symbols have been determined to propagate them to a complete solution. The strategy presented is successful in difficult cases through ranks 11 and 12, including $\operatorname{Z}(\mathrm{Haagerup}_3)$, and does not require the category to be multiplicity-free. Although the algorithm is implemented numerically, we describe a reliable means of recovering the exact $F$-symbols, assuming that in some gauge they lie in a given number field, and of certifying every pentagon and hexagon equation exactly. The exotic rank-11 anisotropic modular category B11-00119 (https://anyonatlas.org/data/B11-00119), with largest fusion coefficient 4, is used as a motivating example, for which the solve takes roughly 10 minutes on a laptop. We will continue to add $F$-symbol solutions to https://AnyonAtlas.org as they are completed.

item.title: Exact Organization of Density Matrices and Entanglement Structure in the Kitaev Spin Liquid
item.description: arXiv:2605.18002v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give an exact form of the density matrix of the spin-1/2 Kitaev spin liquid represented in terms of spin operators and study the entanglement structures of the Kitaev honeycomb model within the spin framework. We show that th…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2605.18002v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give an exact form of the density matrix of the spin-1/2 Kitaev spin liquid represented in terms of spin operators and study the entanglement structures of the Kitaev honeycomb model within the spin framework. We show that the density matrix is naturally organized by equivalence classes of string operators associated with the underlying gauge structure of the model. With the explicit form of the density matrix, plus the exact Gauss law of the emergent gauge theory and the exact 1-form Wilson symmetry in the Kitaev model, we demonstrate the existence of the underlying symmetry-resolved block-diagonal structure of the reduced density matrix, which gives rise to the extensive degeneracy in the entanglement spectrum. The block-diagonal structure is then proven to be responsible for the separability of the entanglement entropy into the gauge and matter parts. Furthermore, we extend the formalism to subsystems with an odd number of lattice sites, revealing a relation between the entanglement spectrum and the fermion parity that is seldom mentioned in the literature.

item.title: Textured phase diagrams of featureless insulators
item.description: arXiv:2605.20339v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study phase diagrams of charge-conserving `class A' non-interacting fermions, focusing on the trivial phase in various dimensions. Such phases are usually termed `featureless' to distinguish them from those others with either…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2605.20339v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study phase diagrams of charge-conserving `class A' non-interacting fermions, focusing on the trivial phase in various dimensions. Such phases are usually termed `featureless' to distinguish them from those others with either symmetry-broken or topological order. We show that the presence of non-trivial topological families of states, including charge pumps and their generalizations, results in phase diagrams being endowed with non-trivial topological textures that can be visualized through Berry phases and their higher-dimensional generalizations. We show that for non-interacting fermion systems with translation invariance, these `higher' Berry phases can be computed using integrals of non-abelian Chern-Simons forms of the Berry-Bloch connection over momentum and parameter spaces. Singularities in these textures correspond to gap-closing loci of `diabolical points', which represent the obstruction to contracting topologically non-trivial families of states, and bulk-boundary correspondence results in a locus of robust boundary modes that terminate at the bulk diabolical points. In the presence of finite chemical potential, we argue that the edge modes are generically robust without any need for fine-tuning for two and higher dimensions, whereas in one dimension they are `estranged' in the phase diagram, i.e. appearing at different parameter values for different edges. We demonstrate our results by constructing several microscopic models of non-interacting fermions. We argue stability to interactions and explore proximate phase diagrams by mapping to continuum field theories.

item.title: On the Relation Between String Order Parameters, Entanglement, and Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions in Topological Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2605.25611v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Topological order is defined by topological invariants, rather than symmetries and local order parameters. Nonetheless some topological phases can be characterized by string order parameters and entanglement. In this article we …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2605.25611v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Topological order is defined by topological invariants, rather than symmetries and local order parameters. Nonetheless some topological phases can be characterized by string order parameters and entanglement. In this article we study how string order parameters and entanglement spectra behave out-of-equilibrium following quenches in one dimensional topological models with $\mathbb{Z}$ invariants. Previously it has been suggested that string order parameters could serve as an experimental probe of dynamical quantum phase transitions. Despite the existence of clear zeroes in the order parameters at critical times, we show that in general there is no exact quantitative or qualitative connection with the critical times of dynamical quantum phase transitions. Another possible connection is of dynamical string order parameter zeroes and dynamical crossings at the center of entanglement spectra. Here we see that there can sometimes be a connection, but it is not typical. Again there is no general quantitative or qualitative connection. Each dynamical form of criticality behaves independently, though we do see that critical times tend to be of the same order of magnitude and give an argument for why this is the case. We also find that a string order parameter which labels one topological phase can undergo non-trivial dynamics even following a quench between \emph{other} topological phases. We elucidate where connections can be made, and where they result from a consideration of insufficiently general models. These results cast doubt on the idea of genuine dynamical phases following quenches in such models.

item.title: Bobkingite, a new coupled sawtooth chain platform
item.description: arXiv:2606.26243v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the mineral bobkingite, $\mathrm{Cu}_5(\mathrm{OH})_8\mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_2$, as a potential realization of the sawtooth chain. Using ab initio methods, we estimate the magnetic exchange couplings…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2606.26243v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the mineral bobkingite, $\mathrm{Cu}_5(\mathrm{OH})_8\mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_2$, as a potential realization of the sawtooth chain. Using ab initio methods, we estimate the magnetic exchange couplings and find that bobkingite hosts quasi-one-dimensional sawtooth chains, with residual three-dimensional interactions strongly suppressed by the crystal geometry. Examining the full exchange network, we find that the classical model exhibits an extensive manifold of nearly degenerate states with emergent two-dimensional character, which spin-wave theory shows to persist as Ising degrees of freedom. Unlike other sawtooth candidates, bobkingite has negligible vertical interchain coupling, preserving a one-dimensional degeneracy even in the presence of ordering, suggesting that any long-range order is weak. Thermal fluctuations stabilize a finite-temperature regime of multiplanar fluctuations rooted in the classical chain degeneracy, whose spin correlations resemble those of the quantum sawtooth chain, suggesting the persistence of quantum features in the full model. This makes bobkingite a compelling platform for exploring sawtooth chain physics.

item.title: Colloquium: Semi-Dirac Fermions in Quantum Matter
item.description: arXiv:2607.20627v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article reviews the recent progress on the subject of semi-Dirac fermions, two dimensional quasiparticles that disperse quadratically, as Galilean invariant particles, or linearly, as massless relativistic particles, depend…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2607.20627v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article reviews the recent progress on the subject of semi-Dirac fermions, two dimensional quasiparticles that disperse quadratically, as Galilean invariant particles, or linearly, as massless relativistic particles, depending on their direction of motion. These quasiparticles exist at phase boundaries set by the continuous change in the connectivity of Fermi surfaces, known as Lifshitz transitions. The basic properties and the current experimental evidence of the existence of these quasiparticles in both synthetic lattices and quantum materials are presented. The many-body problem of semi-Dirac fermions is discussed from a theoretical perspective with an eye to physical observables of relevance to experiments.

item.title: A Perspective on Topological Charge Density Wave Materials
item.description: arXiv:2611.13360v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Charge density waves are among the earliest known ordered states in quantum materials, yet they have re-emerged at the center of modern discussions of topology, symmetry breaking, and collective dynamics. In several material cla…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.13360v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Charge density waves are among the earliest known ordered states in quantum materials, yet they have re-emerged at the center of modern discussions of topology, symmetry breaking, and collective dynamics. In several material classes, charge-density-wave order reshapes electronic bands, boundary states, defect structures, and electromagnetic responses in ways that invite a topological interpretation. Real-space imaging has shown that incommensurate order can form networks of phase defects rather than uniform modulations. Boundary-resolved spectroscopy has revealed in-gap modes whose existence and spatial structure track the charge-density-wave order, although such observations remain confined to a single material family. In Weyl materials, density-wave gaps have been linked to axion-like magnetoelectric response, placing the charge-density-wave phase within a dynamical-field description of the effective action. In kagome metals, charge order is intertwined with Berry curvature, unconventional symmetry breaking, and superconductivity. These developments have led to the term "topological charge density wave," but the phrase describes several physically distinct phenomena. We distinguish three meanings: (i) topology of the order parameter and its defects, (ii) topology of the charge-density-wave-reconstructed electronic structure and its boundary modes, and (iii) axion-like electromagnetic response generated by density-wave order. The experimental and theoretical support for these three meanings differs substantially. This Perspective traces the development of these ideas, clarifies the evidence behind each class, identifies unresolved questions and points of debate, and outlines experimental criteria for establishing topology in charge-density-wave states.

item.title: Symmetry-preserving gapped Dirac state revealed by site-selective $^{13}$C NMR in $\alpha$-(BETS)$_2$I$_3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.16939v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report evidence that the low-temperature insulating phase of $\alpha$-(BETS)$_2$I$_3$ preserves both inversion and time-reversal symmetries using site-selective $^{13}$C nuclear magnetic resonance. $\alpha$-(BETS)$_2$I$_3$ un…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.16939v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report evidence that the low-temperature insulating phase of $\alpha$-(BETS)$_2$I$_3$ preserves both inversion and time-reversal symmetries using site-selective $^{13}$C nuclear magnetic resonance. $\alpha$-(BETS)$_2$I$_3$ undergoes a metal-insulator transition or sharp crossover at approximately 50 K and has been proposed as a candidate spin-orbit-coupling-induced Dirac insulator, yet the nature of its insulating ground state remains unresolved. The NMR spectra exhibit no additional splitting down to 2 K and remain fully described by one quartet and two doublets associated with the three types of molecular sites, A (=A$^{\prime}$), B and C sites, demonstrating the preservation of inversion symmetry. Furthermore, no anomalous line broadening or critical enhancement of the nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate is observed, indicating the absence of magnetic ordering and time-reversal-symmetry breaking. Analysis of the Knight shifts yields site-specific spin susceptibilities satisfying $\chi_{\mathrm{C}} > \chi_{\mathrm{A}} > \chi_{\mathrm{B}}$, a characteristic feature of tilted Dirac-cone electronic states as observed in $\alpha$-(BEDT-TTF)$_2$I$_3$ under pressure. However, the faint field-induced ferrimagnetic-like spin excitations observed in $\alpha$-(BEDT-TTF)$_2$I$_3$, which are ascribed to the gapless tilted Dirac cones, are absent in $\alpha$-(BETS)$_2$I$_3$. These results demonstrate that the insulating ground state of $\alpha$-(BETS)$_2$I$_3$ is a symmetry-preserving gapped Dirac state and provide microscopic constraints on proposed correlated topological phases in this molecular Dirac system.

item.title: Anyon Proliferation at Self-Triality: From a Lattice Model to Adjoint QCD$_3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.17724v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how competitive proliferation among three types of anyons in a self-trial $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ gauge theory can drive symmetry breaking while preserving part of the topological order. We construct a deformatio…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17724v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how competitive proliferation among three types of anyons in a self-trial $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ gauge theory can drive symmetry breaking while preserving part of the topological order. We construct a deformation of the honeycomb color code, a spin model rooted in quantum error correction, with an $S_3$ symmetry that permutes the competing anyons, together with time-reversal and fermionic $\mathbb Z_2^{(1)}$ one-form symmetries. We propose two dual continuum descriptions of this transition. The bosonic description is a $\mathrm{PSU}(3)_3\times\mathrm{Spin}(8)_{-1}$ Chern--Simons--Higgs theory with a real Higgs field in the $(\mathbf8_{\mathrm{adj}},\mathbf8_v)$ representation. Fermion-boson duality gives a particularly simple fermionic dual: $\mathrm{PSU}(3)_{3/2}$ QCD$_3$ with a single adjoint Majorana fermion and gauged fermion parity. Both descriptions match the lattice model's symmetries and proposed phase diagram, connecting double-toric-code order to a symmetry-broken phase with residual toric-code order. The transition is described by Higgs condensation and by a Majorana mass changing sign, respectively. This connection to adjoint QCD$_3$ points to a possible continuous $S_3$-breaking transition from competing anyons, in contrast to the conventional first-order three-state Potts transition from competing local order parameters.

item.title: Strain-induced splitting of the CCDW-NCCDW phase transition in 1T-TaS$_2$
item.description: arXiv:2512.19503v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The effects of uniaxial and biaxial tensile strain on the $\rho_{xx}$ and $\rho_{yy}$ components of the resistivity tensor and the commensurate --- nearly commensurate CDW (CCDW-NCCDW) transition temperature in 1T-TaS$_2$ …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2512.19503v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The effects of uniaxial and biaxial tensile strain on the $\rho_{xx}$ and $\rho_{yy}$ components of the resistivity tensor and the commensurate --- nearly commensurate CDW (CCDW-NCCDW) transition temperature in 1T-TaS$_2$ are studied. At room temperature, uniaxial tensile strain increases the resistivity tensor components by a comparable magnitude both parallel and perpendicular to the strain axis. In the case of biaxial strain, up to 20~K decrease in the CCDW-NCCDW phase transition temperature is observed. In the case of uniaxial strain, a new phase with two different CCDW-NCCDW phase transition temperatures is observed, the splitting exceeds 10 K. The occurrence of such a phase is associated with the transition of the CDW into the commensurate state along the tensile strain direction while maintaining nearly commensurability along the perpendicular one. The results allow to justify various models widely used in analysis of transport properties of 1T-TaS$_2$ in commensurate and nearly commensurate states.

item.title: Electrons Hopping across a Molecular Network: Spectra and Symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2607.14687v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate interacting spinless electrons on finite molecular networks described by a tight-binding Hubbard Hamiltonian. The interplay between network geometry, Coulomb interactions and discrete symmetries is analysed …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2607.14687v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate interacting spinless electrons on finite molecular networks described by a tight-binding Hubbard Hamiltonian. The interplay between network geometry, Coulomb interactions and discrete symmetries is analysed for rings with $L=3,4,5,6$ nodes, filled with one, two or three electrons. Special attention is devoted to the role of the network symmetries in determining the structure of the many-body spectrum and the Mulliken classification of the eigenstates. Using group-theoretical methods, we examine the evolution of the spectra in the presence of an external magnetic flux. The Zeeman effect lifts degeneracies and results in combination with the Coulomb interaction to avoided crossings in symmetry sectors. We identify a qualitatively distinction between systems with an even and odd number of particles. At half-filling, particle-hole symmetry (duality) protects selected symmetry sectors against Zeeman splitting.

item.title: Bogoliubov self-consistent $GW$ and second-order Green's function methods for attractive fermionic interactions
item.description: arXiv:2610.03357v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Describing fermionic systems with attractive interactions, such as superconductors and atomic nuclei, beyond the mean-field level remains a central challenge. In this work, we investigate the performance of Bogoliubov full…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2610.03357v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Describing fermionic systems with attractive interactions, such as superconductors and atomic nuclei, beyond the mean-field level remains a central challenge. In this work, we investigate the performance of Bogoliubov fully self-consistent $GW$ (Bog.~sc$GW$) and second-order Green's function (Bog.~scGF2) methods, implemented within a unified imaginary-time and imaginary-frequency framework. Using two attractive Hubbard lattices ($4\times4$ and $2\times8$) as a model study and benchmarking against full configuration interaction (FCI), we find that, for these systems, Bog.~scGF2 provides a more accurate description than Bog.~sc$GW$. In particular, Bog.~sc$GW$ systematically overestimates the correlation energy, with errors increasing rapidly as the attractive interaction strength grows. These results suggest the importance of exchange contributions in such strongly correlated fermionic systems, even when exchange effects are included only at low order in perturbation theory.

item.title: Geometric limits of quantum recovery across an Ising transition
item.description: arXiv:2611.06215v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: How many physical spins must a receiver retain to recover an unknown qubit? Four Ising duality defects encode a qubit over a common pure bulk ground state in a fixed charge sector. We vary that state at fixed defect geomet…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.06215v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: How many physical spins must a receiver retain to recover an unknown qubit? Four Ising duality defects encode a qubit over a common pure bulk ground state in a fixed charge sector. We vary that state at fixed defect geometry and optimize over preselected spins and joint decoders, taking the infinite-chain limit before increasing defect separation. At every fixed finite positive reference field, exact recovery costs the central spacing plus the shorter outer spacing to leading order. For an error falling as any fixed inverse power of separation, the leading cost is the central spacing in the ordered phase, the shorter outer spacing in the disordered phase and their sum at criticality. Order and disorder records in discarded spins explain the contrast. In a critical benchmark, single-spin measurements, a one-way classical message and an output correction preserve reference entanglement on two separated blocks at budgets where every connected interval is entanglement breaking.

item.title: Generalized Schrieffer-Wolff transformation
item.description: arXiv:2611.22014v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Schrieffer-Wolff transformation (SWT) is a cornerstone of effective-Hamiltonian theory. However, the SWT is predominantly used for weak-coupling problems, while a systematic counterpart for strongly coupled regimes rem…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.22014v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Schrieffer-Wolff transformation (SWT) is a cornerstone of effective-Hamiltonian theory. However, the SWT is predominantly used for weak-coupling problems, while a systematic counterpart for strongly coupled regimes remains largely unexplored. A general closed-form SWT generator and a clear physical principle for gauge fixing remain elusive, obscuring the transformation's underlying structure. We introduce the dual SWT to deal with the strong-coupling problems. The generalized SWT (gSWT) is formulated for any Hermitian operator and block partition. We establish the geodesic principle for its canonical gauge. Furthermore, we derive an exact closed-form solution of the gSWT generator at every order as a finite nested-commutator sum whose only input is the active gap set. Both the geometric and algebraic aspects of the SWT physics are revealed. The gSWT framework is illustrated in two quantum many-body models, the collective spin model and the transverse-field Ising model.

item.title: Critical--localized reentry under periodic spacer control
item.description: arXiv:2611.23796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tracking a fixed fraction of a quasiperiodic spectrum tests whether repeated critical--localized alternation extends over a nonzero spectral weight. We find such alternation in a matched-dimer chain by varying only the spacer on-sit…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.23796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tracking a fixed fraction of a quasiperiodic spectrum tests whether repeated critical--localized alternation extends over a nonzero spectral weight. We find such alternation in a matched-dimer chain by varying only the spacer on-site energies and following a fixed interval of integrated-density-of-states (IDS) labels. An exact Bloch-determinant identity links the physical transfer discriminant to the bands of a periodic reference operator. For the golden cell frequency, we prove that, on a common full-measure set of phases and for every finite value of the spacer control, the physical spectrum in the open reference bands is critical, with purely singular-continuous spectrum and zero Lyapunov exponent, while the spectrum strictly outside the bands is pure point, with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions. Validated IDS bounds certify repeated critical--localized alternation of the same fixed spectral fraction at successive spacer controls. Spacer shifts move the physical levels and reference-band edges at different rates, allowing us to reshape finite-chain return windows and place their endpoints at prescribed controls. An affine recalibration relocates the control family exactly.

item.title: Wegner model in high dimension: singular continuous spectrum from U(1) symmetry breaking and AAT self-consistency
item.description: arXiv:2611.24515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the energy-spectral decomposition of the Wegner one-orbital model in high lattice dimension using ideas from field theory and statistical mechanics. Most notably, we identify a local spectral measure of singular continuou…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.24515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the energy-spectral decomposition of the Wegner one-orbital model in high lattice dimension using ideas from field theory and statistical mechanics. Most notably, we identify a local spectral measure of singular continuous type for the disordered model at the Anderson transition. The key mechanism that leads to a singular continuous spectrum is a novel scenario of spontaneous symmetry breaking, intimately connected to the non-compactness of the global symmetry group of the field theory. While that symmetry breaks down to a compact subgroup in the metallic phase, it spontaneously breaks down to a nilpotent subgroup at criticality. We describe the symmetry-breaking extremal states approximately, by applying the self-consistent theory of localization due to Abou-Chacra, Anderson, and Thouless. The thrust of our work is to provide a field-theoretical foundation for disorder phenomena associated with singular continuous spectra.

item.title: Real-Space Theory of Nonequilibrium Orbital Magnetization in Inhomogeneous Solids
item.description: arXiv:2611.23404v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We put forward a real-space linear-response theory of orbital magnetization induced by a dc electric field in bulk materials lacking translation invariance. Starting from the current response to a slowly varying electromagnetic fi…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.23404v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We put forward a real-space linear-response theory of orbital magnetization induced by a dc electric field in bulk materials lacking translation invariance. Starting from the current response to a slowly varying electromagnetic field, we show that the linear-in-wavevector conductivity tensor of non-interacting electrons in terms of single-particle Green's functions and the velocity and position operators. This provides a gauge-invariant real-space formulation of the long-wavelength non-equilibrium orbital magnetization of both perfect crystals and disordered systems. In the translationally invariant limit, the formalism recovers the established Bloch picture of orbital magneto-electric effects. We implement the formalism using large-scale Chebyshev expansions and illustrate its capabilities on a Haldane model in the presence of spatially uncorrelated disorder.

item.title: Towards Defect Engineering of Orbital Magnetoelectric Effects
item.description: arXiv:2611.23405v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Orbital magnetization is a fundamental measure of time-reversal symmetry breaking in solids that is accessible by experiments. However, unlike the well-studied equilibrium case, the understanding of orbital magnetism resulting fro…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.23405v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Orbital magnetization is a fundamental measure of time-reversal symmetry breaking in solids that is accessible by experiments. However, unlike the well-studied equilibrium case, the understanding of orbital magnetism resulting from external stimuli such as light and electric fields is still in its infancy. Here we employ a novel real-space framework to investigate charge-to-orbital conversion in a metallic orbital antiferromagnet beyond the conventional Bloch-band picture. We find that common point defects give rise to strongly enhanced time-odd magnetoelectric effects and, depending on their local symmetry, further activate otherwise-forbidden time-even responses. Moreover, we introduce a local marker that provides spatially resolved information on the orbital magnetization carried by non-equilibrium states. Real-space maps reveal that point defects create nanoscale hotspots of orbital magnetization leading to a profound modification of the bulk magnetoelectric response, including a sign reversal of the net orbital moment. Our findings may open up the possibility of engineering linear-response orbital moments with atomic-scale precision by point defects and impurities.

item.title: Construction of a Deployable Hard-Constrained Turbulence Closure
item.description: arXiv:2611.23539v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a framework for constructing deployable hard-constrained turbulence closures of unclosed terms in the transport equations of Reynolds stresses and turbulent dissipation rate. The framework is built from modules, each pe…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.23539v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a framework for constructing deployable hard-constrained turbulence closures of unclosed terms in the transport equations of Reynolds stresses and turbulent dissipation rate. The framework is built from modules, each performing a single task. The closure module represents the closure with a small network, while the state module represents the flow state during training. The closure network is coupled to the state network through the governing equation residuals, allowing the closure to be learned without reference closure values being supplied as training data. The coordinate module learns monotone input coordinates that help both networks resolve sharp changes. Within the network architecture, the boundary condition (BC) module imposes boundary values exactly using the Theory of Functional Connections, and the realizability module keeps the closure realizable. We apply the framework to decaying homogeneous isotropic turbulence (HIT) with experimental and direct numerical simulation trajectories. Here, the state module is a Deep Operator Network (DeepONet), the BC module imposes the initial state and the closure's low and high Reynolds number limits, and the realizability module ensures growth of the Taylor microscale. Across ten random seeds, the framework reduces root-mean-square seed-to-seed closure variation by about 95\% relative to the unconstrained model over the training and held-out range. The deployed 18-parameter closure network requires only the Taylor scale Reynolds number and can be exported as a standalone C function.

item.title: Parisi Energy before Parisi Geometry in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
item.description: arXiv:2611.23645v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The fractured low-energy landscape of spin glasses presents a notorious barrier to optimization. While high-depth calculations indicate that the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) can approach the Parisi ground-stat…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.23645v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The fractured low-energy landscape of spin glasses presents a notorious barrier to optimization. While high-depth calculations indicate that the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) can approach the Parisi ground-state energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass, how it does so remains elusive. Here, we treat the QAOA distribution as a statistical-physics object and probe its geometry directly in the thermodynamic limit. We draw two independent bitstrings from the same problem instance and couple them through their macroscopic similarity. We find that typical QAOA samples remain macroscopically uncorrelated, even as their sensitivity to this coupling grows with circuit depth $p$. By contrast, the low-energy tail shows a much stronger tendency to overlap and reveals a Parisi-like phase with the same critical behavior as the thermal spin-glass transition. The onset of this organization moves toward the typical output as the circuit deepens, consistent with the separation vanishing only as $p\to\infty$. Together, these findings suggest a route distinct from structure-exploiting classical algorithms and thermal sampling, one in which the QAOA approaches the Parisi energy before Parisi geometry becomes typical.

item.title: Free energy distribution for two non-crossing directed polymers on the cylinder
item.description: arXiv:2611.23981v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the partition sum $Z_L(t)$ of two non-crossing continuum directed polymers of length $t$, in a common random medium with the geometry of a cylinder of circumference length $L$. In the limit $t \to +\infty$, the $k$-th …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.23981v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the partition sum $Z_L(t)$ of two non-crossing continuum directed polymers of length $t$, in a common random medium with the geometry of a cylinder of circumference length $L$. In the limit $t \to +\infty$, the $k$-th cumulant of (minus) the free energy $\log Z_L(t)$, grows as $c_k(L) t$, and we compute the amplitudes $c_k(L)$. To this aim we first study the integer moments $\langle Z_L(t)^n \rangle$, whose long-time behavior is determined by the ground-state energy of the one-dimensional attractive Lieb--Liniger model in the symmetry sector associated with the Young diagram $(n,n)$ (a two-component bosonic nested Bethe ansatz). This ground state energy is obtained using the nested Bethe-Ansatz involving $2n$ physical rapidities and $n$ auxiliary rapidities. The analytic continuation in the replica number $n$, which yields the cumulants $c_k(L)$, is performed through a non-trivial generalization of the method developed by Brunet and Derrida for a single polymer on the cylinder. We obtain fully explicit formulas for the mean $c_1(L)$ and the variance $c_2(L)$, and construct a systematic scheme for computing all higher cumulants $c_k(L)$. Finally, taking $L\to+\infty$ and $n\to0$ with $nL^{1/2}$ fixed, we derive a universal scaling function which characterizes the large-deviation statistics of the two-polymer free energy and is expected to be universal within the one-dimensional two-layer periodic SHE/KPZ class. The two tails of the large-deviation function are obtained analytically, revealing different roles of the non-crossing constraint in favorable and unfavorable fluctuations of the common disorder.

item.title: Quantum Annealing with a Quantum Neural Network: Width of Annealing Matters
item.description: arXiv:2611.24089v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum annealing is a promising quantum algorithm for dealing with computationally hard optimization problems. Currently available hardware can implement the algorithm for a significant class of Hamiltonian problems. However, its…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.24089v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum annealing is a promising quantum algorithm for dealing with computationally hard optimization problems. Currently available hardware can implement the algorithm for a significant class of Hamiltonian problems. However, its performance is especially limited in discontinuous quantum phase transitions, where the energy gap shrinks exponentially with system size. In this paper, we introduce an extension of quantum annealing to a quantum neural network and study its performance in a number of prototypical optimization problems. In particular, we observe that already a random quantum annealing network of width W = 2 can exponentially reduce the number of evolution layers or depth of the annealing process in the quantum search problem. By tuning the network parameters the search problem can be solved with exponentially small errors by a quantum perceptron of depth L = 1 and width W = 2. The findings show that width of a quantum annealing network is critical to enhance the success probability of the algorithm by providing a larger and learnable evolution space for the annealing process.

item.description: arXiv:2611.24346v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a microscopic framework for the disorder-averaged density-matrix dynamics of pseudospin-$1/2$ systems with anisotropic and nonlinear spin-momentum couplings. Starting from the Diffuson, we introduce a matrix-valued rati…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.24346v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a microscopic framework for the disorder-averaged density-matrix dynamics of pseudospin-$1/2$ systems with anisotropic and nonlinear spin-momentum couplings. Starting from the Diffuson, we introduce a matrix-valued rational approximation for its frequency dependence that does not rely on a low-frequency or weak-coupling expansion. The resulting pole equation is recast as a quadratic eigenvalue problem, from which the real-time evolution of the disorder-averaged density matrix is constructed. We apply the formulation to a two-dimensional electron gas with Rashba and linear and cubic Dresselhaus couplings, a $d$-wave altermagnet with Rashba coupling, and a three-dimensional double-Weyl model. Comparisons with direct numerical simulations demonstrate quantitative agreement for both the post-quench spin dynamics and spin relaxation times across a broad range of coupling strengths, extending beyond the diffusive regime. The matrix-rational formulation provides a unified description of ultrafast spin dynamics and long-time relaxation.
